::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
## Purpose

This document fixes the story of the manuscript: three research questions, the variables that answer them, and the figures that go into the main text and into Appendix S1. Everything not listed here is left out. Figure numbers in this document (Figure 1, 2, …) are its own; the manuscript figure each one becomes is written in bold above it.
:::

# 1. The variables

The subject of every effect statement is **beaver-engineering**, the physical modification beavers create, because the upstream–downstream contrast measures the whole beaver-engineered stream. The unit of analysis is the stream.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-variables
#| tbl-cap: "The derived variables used throughout this document, referenced from every figure caption below."
#| echo: false
kable(tribble(
  ~Symbol, ~Name, ~Definition, ~`Meaning (unit)`, ~`Question it answers`,
  "$\\text{DOC}_{up,s}$, $\\text{DOC}_{down,s}$", "upstream DOC, downstream DOC", "measured",
  "DOC concentration entering / leaving the beaver-engineered stream in season $s$ ($w$ = winter, $s$ = summer) **(mg L$^{-1}$)**",
  "What is the DOC concentration before and after the beaver-engineered stream in each season?",
  "$\\Delta\\text{DOC}_s$", "local response", "$\\text{DOC}_{down,s} - \\text{DOC}_{up,s}$",
  "the change in DOC that beaver-engineering produces in season $s$; positive = enrichment, negative = depletion **(mg L$^{-1}$)**",
  "Does beaver-engineering increase or decrease DOC, and by how much, in each season?",
  "$S$", "inherited seasonal contrast", "$\\text{DOC}_{up,summer} - \\text{DOC}_{up,winter}$",
  "the winter-to-summer change of upstream DOC, i.e. what the upstream river corridor delivers to the stream **(mg L$^{-1}$)**",
  "How much does DOC change between winter and summer in the river before it reaches the beaver-engineered stream?",
  "$R_s$", "relative response", "$\\Delta\\text{DOC}_s / \\lvert S \\rvert$",
  "how much DOC beaver-engineering adds ($R_s > 0$) or removes ($R_s < 0$) in season $s$, as a fraction of the inherited seasonal contrast **(dimensionless)**",
  "How much does beaver-engineering add or remove DOC, relative to the inherited seasonal contrast?",
  "$B$", "beaver seasonal modification", "$\\Delta\\text{DOC}_{summer} - \\Delta\\text{DOC}_{winter}$",
  "how much beaver-engineering changes the winter-to-summer DOC contrast **(mg L$^{-1}$)**",
  "Does beaver-engineering change the seasonal DOC contrast, beyond its effect within each season?",
  "$G$", "seasonal gain", "$B / S$",
  "$G > 0$: beaver-engineering **reinforces** the inherited seasonal contrast; $-1 < G < 0$: **dampens** it; $G < -1$: **reverses** it **(dimensionless)**",
  "Does beaver-engineering reinforce, dampen or reverse the inherited seasonal contrast?",
  "$A_\\text{beaver}$, $A_\\text{floodplain}$", "areas", "mapped",
  "ponded footprint of the beaver-engineered stream; contributing catchment floodplain area **(km$^2$)**",
  "How large is the beaver-engineered footprint, and how large is the floodplain that generates $S$?",
  "$F$", "footprint contrast", "$A_\\text{floodplain} / A_\\text{beaver}$",
  "how much larger the floodplain area is than the beaver-engineered footprint **(dimensionless)**",
  "How small is the beaver-engineered footprint relative to the floodplain that generates $S$?"))
```

# 2. Research questions and hypotheses

**Q1 — Direction.** *Does beaver-engineering consistently increase or decrease DOC downstream compared with upstream?*
Hypothesis: if a stream is impounded by beaver dams, then the local response $\Delta\text{DOC}_s$ will not have a consistent sign across streams, because impoundment simultaneously starts DOC-producing processes — exudation and senescence of phytoplankton and macrophytes, leaching of litter and inundated soils [@søndergaard1985; @sell1992; @aitkenhead1999] — and DOC-removing processes — microbial mineralization, photodegradation and sedimentation during the longer residence time [@johnston2017; @nummi2018] — whose balance depends on the stream; syntheses accordingly report enrichment, no change and depletion [@larsen2021; @grudzinski2022]. We further expect the balance to tilt toward enrichment in summer, when production exceeds removal [@mulholland1997].

**Q2 — Drivers.** *Which abiotic and biotic drivers set the direction of the local response?*
Hypothesis: if the number of dams increases, then water residence time increases because each dam impounds water and slows flow [@westbrook2006; @majerova2015]; if water residence time and solar radiation increase, then phytoplankton and macrophyte abundance increase because nutrients are retained and light is available for photosynthesis [@reynolds2006; @finger2007; @feuchtmayr2009]; if primary producer abundance and soil litter cover increase, then $\Delta\text{DOC}_s$ increases because exudation, senescence and litter leaching release DOC [@reitsema2018; @gessner1999]; if upstream DOC increases, then $\Delta\text{DOC}_s$ decreases because a larger incoming load is proportionally retained or mineralized within the pond [@larson2007; @wohl2013]. The thirteen path-specific hypotheses are in Appendix S1, Table S1.

**Q3 — Magnitude and seasonal modification.** *How much does beaver-engineering add or remove DOC relative to the inherited seasonal contrast, and does it reinforce, dampen or reverse that contrast?*
Hypothesis, magnitude: if the season is summer, then the relative response $R_{summer}$ will be positive and a substantial fraction of the inherited seasonal contrast, because higher light and temperature raise autochthonous DOC production inside the pond independently of the upstream corridor [@mulholland1997; @battin2023]; if the season is winter, then $R_{winter}$ will be close to zero because primary production is minimal.
Hypothesis, modification: if the summer response exceeds the winter response ($B > 0$ where $S > 0$), then the seasonal gain $G$ will be positive and beaver-engineering will reinforce the inherited seasonal contrast; because the balance of DOC-producing and DOC-removing processes is stream-specific (Q1), we expect $G$ to be heterogeneous across streams, with reinforcement, dampening and reversal all present.
Because $A_\text{beaver}$ is a very small part of $A_\text{floodplain}$ (footprint contrast $F \gg 1$), both responses arise on a footprint far smaller than the corridor that generates $S$.

**Q4 — Intensity.** *Does the local response scale with the intensity of beaver-engineering — the number of dams and the water residence time — or is it organised by something else?*
Hypothesis: if the number of dams and the water residence time increase, then $R_{summer}$ and $G$ will become more positive, because longer impoundment retains nutrients and creates habitat for the primary producers that add DOC in summer [@westbrook2006; @majerova2015; @feuchtmayr2009]. Because Q2 found only weak paths from the dams through water residence time, we expect at most a weak ordering of the streams along these gradients. Q4 is descriptive and belongs in Appendix S1; it answers the question a reader asks after Figure 4: "are the streams on the right the ones with more dams?"

**Q5 — Mechanism of the sign.** *Why do some beaver-engineered streams enrich and others deplete DOC, and why does the same stream change role between seasons?*
Hypothesis: if enrichment occurs where the biological and organic-matter pathways of the SCM (phytoplankton, macrophytes, litter) contribute most, and depletion where these contributions are weak and removal dominates, then decomposing the SCM's predicted local modification into pathway contributions will separate sources from sinks, and the summer-minus-winter change of the producer contributions will track the beaver seasonal modification $B$ [@mulholland1997; @battin2023]. Removal processes (mineralization, photodegradation) were not measured, so whatever the measured pathways cannot explain is reported as an unresolved component, not attributed.

The division of labour between the two quantities is fixed: **$R_s$ answers "how much, in season $s$" (Figure 2a, b); $G$ answers "what does that do to the seasonal contrast itself" (Figure 2c)**.

# 3. Q1 — Direction

**Manuscript placement: main text, Figure 1a (existing, unchanged).**

![**Direction of the local response.** Posterior predictive distribution of $\Delta\text{DOC}_s$ for a single sampling of a beaver-engineered stream, in winter and summer, from the measurement-error model on the raw upstream and downstream concentrations. Coral: posterior predictive probability of a sink response ($\Delta\text{DOC}_s < -0.5$ mg L$^{-1}$); grey: negligible response (ROPE $\pm 0.5$ mg L$^{-1}$); skyblue: source response ($\Delta\text{DOC}_s > 0.5$ mg L$^{-1}$). Point: median; bars: 66% and 95% intervals. $\Delta\text{DOC}_s$ is defined in @tbl-variables.](../../overleaf/figures/media/Figure_2a.png){#fig-q1}

```{r q1-data}
# raw data: one row per sampling; pair each stream's winter and summer sampling
m <- read.csv(here("data", "processed", "m12.csv"))
w <- m |> filter(season == "winter") |> select(site, beaver_territory, up_w = DOC_input, dn_w = DOC_out,
                                                 Afp = A_floodplain_km2, Abv = A_beaver_km2)
s <- m |> filter(season == "summer") |> select(site, beaver_territory, up_s = DOC_input, dn_s = DOC_out)
# the 158 streams with both seasons complete; local responses and footprint contrast
d <- inner_join(w, s, by = c("site", "beaver_territory")) |> filter(complete.cases(up_w, dn_w, up_s, dn_s)) |>
  mutate(dw = dn_w - up_w,      # local response in winter
         ds = dn_s - up_s,      # local response in summer
         F  = Afp / Abv)        # footprint contrast
# shares of enrichment by season, and streams that switch direction between seasons
sw <- d |> summarise(n = n(), winter_enrich = mean(dw > 0), summer_enrich = mean(ds > 0),
                     dep_to_enr = sum(dw < 0 & ds > 0), enr_to_dep = sum(dw > 0 & ds < 0))
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Key message of @fig-q1

-   **Average local response: negligible.** +0.14 mg L$^{-1}$ in summer, 0.00 mg L$^{-1}$ in winter, both inside the ROPE of $\pm$0.5 mg L$^{-1}$.
-   **One sampling of one stream is highly variable.** Winter: 77% negligible, 11% source, 12% sink; summer: 75% negligible, 15% source, 9% sink (posterior predictive shares).
-   **Across the `r sw$n` streams:** `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100*sw$winter_enrich)` show enrichment in winter and `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100*sw$summer_enrich)` in summer; `r sw$dep_to_enr` switch from winter depletion to summer enrichment, `r sw$enr_to_dep` the other way.
-   **Implication.** Beaver-engineering has no consistent direction: it is not a DOC source or a DOC sink but a control point whose sign is set locally, with a summer tilt toward release. A single field visit will most often find no ecologically relevant change — which explains the contradictory site studies in the literature.
:::

# 4. Q2 — Drivers

**Manuscript placement: main text, Figure 4 (new, standalone — promoted from panel (b) of Figure 2, given the added causal links from upstream DOC to the primary producers and upstream DOC's own measurement error; Figure 2 keeps only its direction panel).**

The chunk below draws the structural causal model as it will appear in the manuscript, using the model comparison in `notebook/correspondence/scm_outcome_choice.qmd`. The layout is fixed by hand (node positions and edge routing); the numbers are the posterior mean effects of model `downstream_DOC_me` (`notebook/fitting/me_refits.R`) — the same downstream-DOC SCM as before, refit with a latent (measurement-error-corrected) upstream DOC and two additional links, upstream DOC → macrophytes and upstream DOC → phytoplankton, testing whether the incoming DOC also shapes the local response indirectly through the producers. Each edge's line type encodes the posterior probability of its direction; the two new links are drawn in dark red.

```{r dag-draw-fn}
#| echo: false
ME <- readRDS(here("results", "me_refits.rds")); tO <- ME$down$tab
gme <- function(tb, par) tb[tb$par == par, ]
draw_dag <- function(tb, outcome, pref, up, up_lab, title) {
  nodes <- data.frame(name = c("Max dam\nheight", "Number of\ndams", "Channel\ngradient", "Water\nresidence time", "Solar\nradiation", "Macrophytes", "Phytoplankton", "Soil litter\ncover", up_lab, outcome),
    x = c(0.9, 0.9, 2.9, 3.2, 4.6, 6.6, 6.2, 6.2, 8.8, 8.8), y = c(6.6, 4.6, 2.0, 5.0, 9.3, 7.2, 5.0, 2.9, 8.8, 5.4))
  rownames(nodes) <- c("dh", "nd", "gr", "wrt", "sol", "mac", "pla", "lit", "up", "out")
  ed <- function(from, to, par, curv = 0, lx = 0, ly = 0.3, new = FALSE) { g <- gme(tb, par)
    tibble(from = from, to = to, label = sprintf("%.2f", g$mean), class = if (new) "new" else if (g$p_pos > 0.9) "pos" else if (g$p_pos < 0.1) "neg" else "none",
           solid = g$p_pos > 0.9 | g$p_pos < 0.1, curv = curv, lx = lx, ly = ly) }
  edges <- bind_rows(
    ed("dh", "wrt", "bsp_waterrestimez_midam_height_z"), ed("nd", "wrt", "b_waterrestimez_n_dams_z", lx = -0.1, ly = 0.35),
    ed("gr", "wrt", "b_waterrestimez_slope_z", lx = 0.45, ly = 0), ed("wrt", "pla", "bsp_planktonabunz_miwater_res_time_z"),
    ed("wrt", "mac", "bsp_macrophyabunz_miwater_res_time_z"), ed("wrt", "out", paste0("bsp_", pref, "_miwater_res_time_z"), curv = 0.18),
    ed("sol", "mac", "bsp_macrophyabunz_misolar_z", curv = -0.15, lx = 0.55, ly = 0.55), ed("sol", "pla", "bsp_planktonabunz_misolar_z", curv = 0.30, lx = -0.85, ly = 0.1),
    ed("sol", "lit", "bsp_coverlitterz_misolar_z", curv = 0.30), ed("mac", "out", paste0("bsp_", pref, "_mimacrophy_abun_z"), ly = 0.32),
    ed("pla", "out", paste0("bsp_", pref, "_miplankton_abun_z"), ly = 0.30), ed("lit", "out", paste0("bsp_", pref, "_micover_litter_z"), lx = -0.2, ly = 0.32),
    ed("up", "out", paste0("bsp_", pref, "_mi", up), lx = 0.45, ly = 0),
    ed("up", "mac", paste0("bsp_macrophyabunz_mi", up), curv = 0.25, lx = 0.35, ly = 0.35, new = TRUE),
    ed("up", "pla", paste0("bsp_planktonabunz_mi", up), curv = -0.35, lx = -0.9, ly = -0.9, new = TRUE))
  edges$label[!edges$solid & edges$class != "new"] <- ""
  a <- merge(edges, nodes, by.x = "from", by.y = "row.names"); a <- merge(a, nodes, by.x = "to", by.y = "row.names", suffixes = c("", "2"))
  dx <- a$x2 - a$x; dy <- a$y2 - a$y; L <- sqrt(dx^2 + dy^2)
  a$x0 <- a$x + dx / L * 0.85; a$y0 <- a$y + dy / L * 0.55; a$x1 <- a$x2 - dx / L * 0.90; a$y1 <- a$y2 - dy / L * 0.55
  a$xm <- (a$x0 + a$x1) / 2 + a$lx; a$ym <- (a$y0 + a$y1) / 2 + a$ly
  pal <- c(pos = "#3B9AD1", neg = "#E8603C", none = "grey55", new = "#8B0000"); arr <- arrow(length = unit(0.16, "cm"), type = "closed")
  pd <- ggplot()
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(a))) { lt <- if (a$class[i] == "new") (if (a$solid[i]) "solid" else "dotted") else if (a$solid[i]) "solid" else "dashed"
    pd <- pd + if (a$curv[i] == 0) geom_segment(data = a[i, ], aes(x = x0, y = y0, xend = x1, yend = y1), colour = pal[a$class[i]], linetype = lt, linewidth = 0.7, arrow = arr) else
      geom_curve(data = a[i, ], aes(x = x0, y = y0, xend = x1, yend = y1), curvature = a$curv[i], colour = pal[a$class[i]], linetype = lt, linewidth = 0.7, arrow = arr) }
  pd + geom_text(data = subset(a, label != ""), aes(x = xm, y = ym, label = label, colour = class), size = 4.2, show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(pos = "black", neg = "black", none = "black", new = "#8B0000")) +
    geom_label(data = nodes[rownames(nodes) != "out", ], aes(x = x, y = y, label = name), size = 4.1, label.padding = unit(0.3, "lines"), label.r = unit(0.05, "lines")) +
    geom_label(data = nodes["out", ], aes(x = x, y = y, label = name), size = 4.4, fontface = "bold", label.padding = unit(0.45, "lines"), label.r = unit(0.9, "lines"), linewidth = 0.9, colour = "#C0208E") +
    annotate("text", x = 0.15, y = 9.8, label = title, size = 6.5, hjust = 0) +
    xlim(0, 10) + ylim(1.2, 10) + theme_void()
}
```

```{r fig-q2}
#| fig-height: 5.6
#| fig-cap: "**Drivers of downstream DOC.** Structural causal model with downstream DOC as the outcome (model `downstream_DOC_me`) and the posterior mean standardized effects; the upstream-DOC path is the inheritance slope (0.94, mg per mg). Skyblue: positive and coral: negative effects with posterior probability above 0.90; dashed grey: no-evidence. Dark red: the two added links, upstream DOC → macrophytes and → phytoplankton (per mg L⁻¹ of upstream DOC); solid dark red meets the same 0.90 threshold, dotted does not."
pq2 <- draw_dag(tO, "Downstream\nDOC", "DOCout", "DOC_input", "Upstream\nDOC", "")
ggsave(here("images", "Figure_1b_downstream.png"), pq2, width = 9, height = 5.6, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
pq2
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Key message of @fig-q2

-   **Inheritance dominates.** Downstream DOC carries `r sprintf("%.2f", gme(tO,"bsp_DOCout_miDOC_input")$mean)` mg per mg of upstream DOC (P > 0 ≈ 1) — by far the largest path.
-   **Local modification through biology.** Phytoplankton +`r sprintf("%.2f", gme(tO,"bsp_DOCout_miplankton_abun_z")$mean)`, macrophytes +`r sprintf("%.2f", gme(tO,"bsp_DOCout_mimacrophy_abun_z")$mean)`, soil litter +`r sprintf("%.2f", gme(tO,"bsp_DOCout_micover_litter_z")$mean)` (standardized effects on downstream DOC); solar radiation feeds the producers (+`r sprintf("%.2f", gme(tO,"bsp_planktonabunz_misolar_z")$mean)` phytoplankton, +`r sprintf("%.2f", gme(tO,"bsp_macrophyabunz_misolar_z")$mean)` macrophytes).
-   **The dams act only indirectly and weakly.** Number of dams +`r sprintf("%.2f", gme(tO,"b_waterrestimez_n_dams_z")$mean)` and channel gradient `r sprintf("%.2f", gme(tO,"b_waterrestimez_slope_z")$mean)` on water residence time; residence time +`r sprintf("%.2f", gme(tO,"bsp_planktonabunz_miwater_res_time_z")$mean)` on phytoplankton; no direct residence-time → DOC path.
-   **The incoming DOC also reaches the producers, macrophytes only.** Upstream DOC → macrophytes `r sprintf("%.2f", gme(tO,"bsp_macrophyabunz_miDOC_input")$mean)` per mg L⁻¹ (P > 0 = `r sprintf("%.2f", gme(tO,"bsp_macrophyabunz_miDOC_input")$p_pos)`); upstream DOC → phytoplankton `r sprintf("%.2f", gme(tO,"bsp_planktonabunz_miDOC_input")$mean)` (P > 0 = `r sprintf("%.2f", gme(tO,"bsp_planktonabunz_miDOC_input")$p_pos)`, no-evidence) — a DOC-rich inflow goes with more macrophytes, not more phytoplankton.
-   **Implication.** A beaver-engineered stream inherits its DOC and then adds to it; the addition is decided by light and primary producers, not by the size of the engineering, and a richer inflow itself feeds the macrophytes a little further. The producer effects are prior-informed (16 summer streams; section 9) and should be presented as such.
:::

**Parameterization.** The structural causal model is reported with **downstream DOC as the outcome**: upstream DOC enters as a latent true concentration (its reading carries a 0.2 mg L$^{-1}$ instrument error) with a freely estimated inheritance slope, and $\Delta\text{DOC}_s$ is computed from the posterior afterwards as $\text{DOC}_{down,s} - \text{DOC}_{up,s}$, so upstream DOC is never both a predictor and part of the outcome. This reading replaces the older wording of Q2, which described the upstream-DOC path as upstream DOC *causing greater retention*; downstream DOC instead **inherits** the upstream state (slope `r sprintf("%.2f", gme(tO,"bsp_DOCout_miDOC_input")$mean)` mg per mg), and the hydrological/biological pathways are local modifications around that inherited background, not retention of it. Two causal links complete the picture: upstream DOC also feeds the primary producers directly, tested by adding upstream DOC → macrophytes and upstream DOC → phytoplankton to the DAG (supported for macrophytes, not for phytoplankton, above). This model (`downstream_DOC_me`, fit in `notebook/fitting/me_refits.R`, compared against the ΔDOC parameterization in `notebook/correspondence/scm_outcome_choice.qmd`) is the $\Delta$DOC model in a different parameterization: every mediator effect agrees to the second decimal, and the upstream-DOC path is re-read as an inheritance slope of **`r sprintf("%.2f", gme(tO,"bsp_DOCout_miDOC_input")$mean)` [`r sprintf("%.2f", gme(tO,"bsp_DOCout_miDOC_input")$lo)`, `r sprintf("%.2f", gme(tO,"bsp_DOCout_miDOC_input")$hi)`]** — downstream DOC inherits `r sprintf("%.0f", 100*gme(tO,"bsp_DOCout_miDOC_input")$mean)`% of the upstream concentration, mg per mg. Figure 4 (@fig-q2) replaces the former panel (b) of Figure 2; the Methods gain one sentence stating the parameterization, the inheritance slope, and the two added producer links.

**Robustness check: does fixing the inheritance slope at 1 change anything else?** `downstream_DOC_me` estimates the slope freely (prior Normal(1, 0.3), posterior `r sprintf("%.2f", gme(tO,"bsp_DOCout_miDOC_input")$mean)`). A second fit, `downstream_DOC_me_fixed` (`notebook/fitting/downstream_DOC_me_fixed_fit.R`), pins it at 1 (prior Normal(1, 0.001), the standard way to fix an `mi()` coefficient in brms) and is otherwise identical, including the two upstream → producer links and the upstream measurement error.

```{r robustness-inheritance}
#| echo: false
fx_path <- here("results", "models_fit", "downstream_DOC_me_fixed.rds")
if (file.exists(fx_path)) {
  library(brms)
  fit_free <- readRDS(here("results", "models_fit", "downstream_DOC_me.rds")); fit_fix <- readRDS(fx_path)
  d_free <- as_draws_df(fit_free); d_fix  <- as_draws_df(fit_fix)
  qf2 <- function(x) sprintf("%.3f [%.3f, %.3f]", mean(x), quantile(x, .025), quantile(x, .975))
  rob <- tribble(
    ~Parameter, ~`Free slope (downstream_DOC_me)`, ~`Fixed at 1 (downstream_DOC_me_fixed)`,
    "Inheritance slope",  qf2(d_free$bsp_DOCout_miDOC_input),      qf2(d_fix$bsp_DOCout_miDOC_input),
    "Macrophytes",        qf2(d_free$bsp_DOCout_mimacrophy_abun_z), qf2(d_fix$bsp_DOCout_mimacrophy_abun_z),
    "Phytoplankton",      qf2(d_free$bsp_DOCout_miplankton_abun_z), qf2(d_fix$bsp_DOCout_miplankton_abun_z),
    "Soil litter cover",  qf2(d_free$bsp_DOCout_micover_litter_z),  qf2(d_fix$bsp_DOCout_micover_litter_z),
    "Water residence time", qf2(d_free$bsp_DOCout_miwater_res_time_z), qf2(d_fix$bsp_DOCout_miwater_res_time_z),
    "Upstream DOC → macrophytes", qf2(d_free$bsp_macrophyabunz_miDOC_input), qf2(d_fix$bsp_macrophyabunz_miDOC_input),
    "Upstream DOC → phytoplankton", qf2(d_free$bsp_planktonabunz_miDOC_input), qf2(d_fix$bsp_planktonabunz_miDOC_input),
    "Intercept",          qf2(d_free$b_DOCout_Intercept),           qf2(d_fix$b_DOCout_Intercept))
  kable(rob, caption = "Posterior mean [95% CrI]. Fixing the inheritance slope at 1 is a robustness check, not a preferred model.")
  # largest shift among the mediator/producer-link paths, free vs fixed
  shift_pars <- c("bsp_DOCout_mimacrophy_abun_z", "bsp_DOCout_miplankton_abun_z", "bsp_DOCout_micover_litter_z",
                   "bsp_DOCout_miwater_res_time_z", "bsp_macrophyabunz_miDOC_input", "bsp_planktonabunz_miDOC_input")
  shift_lab <- c(bsp_DOCout_mimacrophy_abun_z = "macrophytes", bsp_DOCout_miplankton_abun_z = "phytoplankton",
                 bsp_DOCout_micover_litter_z = "soil litter cover", bsp_DOCout_miwater_res_time_z = "water residence time",
                 bsp_macrophyabunz_miDOC_input = "upstream DOC → macrophytes", bsp_planktonabunz_miDOC_input = "upstream DOC → phytoplankton")
  shifts <- sapply(shift_pars, function(p) abs(mean(d_free[[p]]) - mean(d_fix[[p]])))
  worst <- names(which.max(shifts))
  rob_msg <- sprintf("Both fits converge cleanly (max R-hat %.2f and %.2f). Every mediator effect and both upstream → producer links agree within their credible intervals whether the inheritance slope is estimated freely (%.2f) or pinned at 1 — the largest shift is %s, %.3f to %.3f. Only the intercept moves (%.2f to %.2f), which is expected: fixing the slope at exactly 1 forces the intercept to absorb the small remaining offset.",
    max(rhat(fit_free), na.rm = TRUE), max(rhat(fit_fix), na.rm = TRUE), mean(d_free$bsp_DOCout_miDOC_input),
    shift_lab[worst], mean(d_free[[worst]]), mean(d_fix[[worst]]), mean(d_free$b_DOCout_Intercept), mean(d_fix$b_DOCout_Intercept))
} else { rob_msg <- "pending"
  cat("Fit in progress (notebook/fitting/downstream_DOC_me_fixed_fit.R) -- table will appear once results/models_fit/downstream_DOC_me_fixed.rds exists.")
}
```

**Result: fixing the slope changes nothing else.** `r rob_msg` The mediator story of Figure 4 does not depend on which value the inheritance slope takes.

# 5. Q3 — Magnitude and seasonal modification: $R_s$ and $G$

The analysis uses the **158 streams with both a winter and a summer sampling**.

$R_s$, $B$ and $G$ are computed from posterior draws of each stream's concentrations (Bayesian measurement-error model, `notebook/concentrations_fit.qmd`; the model belongs in the Methods), so no derived quantity is ever formed from raw values and the uncertainty is carried through (`r nrow(readRDS(here("results","concentrations_thin.rds"))$S)` posterior draws per stream).

```{r q3-compute}
# LR holds one matrix per quantity: rows = 4000 posterior draws, columns = 158 streams
LR <- readRDS(here("results", "concentrations_thin.rds"))
R_s <- LR$R_s   # relative response in summer, per draw and stream
R_w <- LR$R_w   # relative response in winter
S_m <- LR$S     # inherited seasonal contrast
# medR: for each posterior draw, the median across streams -> a posterior
# distribution of the across-stream median (optionally on a subset of streams)
medR <- function(R, keep = rep(TRUE, ncol(R))) apply(R[, keep, drop = FALSE], 1, median)
# per-stream median |S|, used only for the small-denominator stability check
absS <- apply(abs(S_m), 2, median)
# qf: format a posterior as "median [95% credible interval]"
qf   <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", median(x), quantile(x, .025), quantile(x, .975))
q3 <- tibble(
  Quantity = c("Median $R_{summer}$ across streams", "Median $R_{winter}$ across streams", "$R_{summer} - R_{winter}$",
               "Median $R_{summer}$, excluding the 20% smallest $\\lvert S \\rvert$ (ratio-stability check)"),
  `Posterior median [95% CrI]` = c(qf(medR(R_s)), qf(medR(R_w)), qf(medR(R_s) - medR(R_w)), qf(medR(R_s, absS > quantile(absS, .2)))),
  `P(> 0)` = sprintf("%.3f", c(mean(medR(R_s) > 0), mean(medR(R_w) > 0), mean(medR(R_s) - medR(R_w) > 0),
                               mean(medR(R_s, absS > quantile(absS, .2)) > 0))))
kable(q3)
# streams whose summer relative response is positive (or negative) with P > 0.90
n_add <- sum(colMeans(R_s > 0) > 0.90); n_rem <- sum(colMeans(R_s < 0) > 0.90); n_str <- ncol(R_s)
# Seasonal gain G = B / S, per stream, from the same posterior draws
# beaver seasonal modification B = summer response - winter response, per draw
B_m <- LR$ds - LR$dw
# seasonal gain G = B / S: does beaver-engineering reinforce (G > 0),
# dampen (-1 < G < 0) or reverse (G < -1) the inherited seasonal contrast?
G_m <- B_m / S_m
g_med <- median(apply(G_m, 1, function(g) median(g)))  # posterior median of the across-stream median gain
```

**Manuscript placement: main text, Figure 2 (new; replaces the amplification-factor figure).**

```{r fig-R}
#| fig-height: 12.5
#| fig-cap: "**Relative response $R_s$ and seasonal gain $G$ of beaver-engineering.** (a) Posterior distribution of the median relative response across the 158 streams, in winter and summer; point: posterior median, bars: 66% and 95% credible intervals; dashed line: no response. (b) Relative response of each stream in summer: posterior median with 66% (thick) and 95% (thin) credible intervals, streams ranked by their median; the grey band marks $\\lvert R_{summer} \\rvert < 0.1$. The vertical axis is linear between $-0.1$ and $0.1$ and logarithmic beyond, so small and large responses are both readable. In panels (a) and (b) skyblue: source (beaver-engineering adds DOC, P > 0.90), coral: sink (removes DOC, P > 0.90), grey: no-evidence — the same colours as in the direction figure; panel (b) prints the percentage of the 158 streams in each colour directly on the plot. (c) Out of the 158 streams, what percentage reinforce ($G > 0$, make the inherited seasonal contrast bigger), dampen ($-1 < G < 0$, make it smaller) or reverse ($G < -1$, flip its sign)? Each stream is classified on every posterior draw, so each bar is a full posterior distribution of that percentage, with its own uncertainty — not a single count of streams sorted into fixed bins; point: posterior median percentage, bars: 66% and 95% credible intervals. $R_s$, $G$, $B$ and $S$ are defined in @tbl-variables."
# classify by posterior probability: add if P(R > 0) > 0.90, remove if P(R < 0) > 0.90, else no-evidence
cls <- function(p_add) case_when(p_add > 0.90 ~ "add", p_add < 0.10 ~ "remove", TRUE ~ "none")
lab <- c(add = "source (adds DOC)", remove = "sink (removes DOC)", none = "no-evidence")   # P > 0.90 stated once, in the caption

# ---- panel (a): across-stream median, winter and summer --------------------
pop <- bind_rows(tibble(season = "summer", v = medR(R_s)), tibble(season = "winter", v = medR(R_w))) |>
  mutate(season = factor(season, levels = c("winter", "summer"))) |>
  group_by(season) |> mutate(class = cls(mean(v > 0))) |> ungroup()
pa <- ggplot(pop, aes(x = v, y = season, fill = class)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey45") +
  stat_halfeye(.width = c(.66, .95), point_interval = "median_qi", alpha = .9) +  # 66% and 95% intervals
  scale_fill_manual(values = PAL, labels = lab, breaks = names(lab), name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
  labs(x = expression("Median relative response across streams,  "*R[s]*" = "*Delta*DOC[s]*" / |S|"), y = NULL) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "top")

# ---- panel (b): each stream's summer relative response, ranked -------------
# per stream: posterior median, 66% and 95% credible intervals, and its class
per <- tibble(med  = apply(R_s, 2, median),
              lo95 = apply(R_s, 2, quantile, .025), hi95 = apply(R_s, 2, quantile, .975),
              lo66 = apply(R_s, 2, quantile, .17),  hi66 = apply(R_s, 2, quantile, .83),
              class = cls(colMeans(R_s > 0))) |> arrange(med) |> mutate(rank = row_number())
# percentage of the 158 streams in each colour: the legend names the colour,
# the in-panel text gives its share (top-left corner is empty of points)
pct_b <- prop.table(table(factor(per$class, levels = c("add", "remove", "none")))) * 100
pct_lab <- tibble(class = c("add", "remove", "none"),
                   txt = sprintf("%.0f%% of streams", pct_b[c("add", "remove", "none")]),
                   y = c(90, 30, 10))   # stacked top to bottom on the log axis
# axis transform: linear inside [-0.1, 0.1], logarithmic beyond
psl <- pseudo_log_trans(sigma = 0.1, base = 10)
pb <- ggplot(per, aes(x = rank, y = med, colour = class)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = -0.1, ymax = 0.1, fill = "grey88", alpha = .8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey45") +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lo95, ymax = hi95), alpha = .45, linewidth = 0.4) +  # 95% interval (thin)
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lo66, ymax = hi66), alpha = .8, linewidth = 0.9) +   # 66% interval (thick)
  geom_point(size = 1.6) +
  geom_text(data = pct_lab, aes(x = 3, y = y, label = txt, colour = class), hjust = 0, size = 4, fontface = "bold", show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(add = "#3B9AD1", remove = "#E8603C", none = "grey60"), labels = lab, breaks = names(lab), name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(trans = psl, breaks = c(-10, -1, -0.1, 0, 0.1, 1, 10)) +
  labs(x = "Stream", y = expression(R[summer]*" = "*Delta*DOC[summer]*" / |S|")) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "top")
# ---- panel (c): posterior share of streams that reinforce/dampen/reverse ---
# classify every stream on EVERY posterior draw (no P > 0.90 threshold), then
# compute the proportion in each zone per draw -- this gives a posterior
# distribution of the proportion itself, propagating its own uncertainty,
# rather than a single count built from per-stream point classifications.
zone <- function(g) case_when(g > 0 ~ "reinforce", g > -1 ~ "dampen", TRUE ~ "reverse")
zmat <- apply(G_m, c(1, 2), zone)                       # same shape as G_m, one label per draw x stream
gprop <- as_tibble(t(apply(zmat, 1, function(row)        # proportion per zone, one row per draw
  c(reinforce = mean(row == "reinforce"), dampen = mean(row == "dampen"), reverse = mean(row == "reverse"))))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "zone", values_to = "p") |>
  mutate(zone = factor(zone, levels = c("reverse", "dampen", "reinforce")))
gpal <- c(reinforce = "#8856A7", dampen = "#41AB5D", reverse = "#B5651D")   # light brown
pc <- ggplot(gprop, aes(x = p, y = zone, fill = zone)) +
  stat_halfeye(.width = c(.66, .95), point_interval = "median_qi") +   # 66% and 95% credible intervals
  scale_fill_manual(values = gpal, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_percent(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Percentage of the 158 streams", y = expression("Seasonal gain,  "*G*" = "*B*" / "*S)) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
fig2 <- pa / pb / pc + plot_layout(heights = c(1, 1.3, 1)) + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a")
ggsave(here("results", "figures", "plan", "fig_R.png"), fig2, width = 9, height = 11, dpi = 300)
fig2
# summary of panel (c) for the key message, one row per zone
gsum <- gprop |> group_by(zone) |> summarise(med = median(p), lo = quantile(p, .025), hi = quantile(p, .975))
gz <- function(z) gsum |> filter(zone == z)

# same +/-0.1 ROPE as panel (b)'s grey band, applied to R_summer, to compare
# against @fig-q1's ROPE logic (see the note below)
zone_r <- function(r) case_when(r > 0.1 ~ "source", r < -0.1 ~ "sink", TRUE ~ "negligible")
rzmat <- apply(R_s, c(1, 2), zone_r)
rprop <- as_tibble(t(apply(rzmat, 1, function(row)
  c(source = mean(row == "source"), negligible = mean(row == "negligible"), sink = mean(row == "sink"))))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "zone", values_to = "p")
rz <- function(z) rprop |> filter(zone == z) |> summarise(med = median(p))
```

::: {.callout-important}
## Key message of @fig-R

-   **(a) Magnitude.** Winter: relative response `r sprintf("%.2f", median(medR(R_w)))` — nothing added. Summer: beaver-engineering adds DOC equal to `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100*median(medR(R_s)))` of the inherited seasonal contrast $S$ (95% CrI `r sprintf("%.0f–%.0f%%", 100*quantile(medR(R_s), .025), 100*quantile(medR(R_s), .975))`).
-   **(b) Heterogeneity.** In summer `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * n_add / n_str)` of streams (`r n_add` of `r n_str`) are DOC sources, `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * n_rem / n_str)` (`r n_rem`) are sinks, the rest no-evidence.
-   **(c) Seasonal gain.** `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100*gz("reinforce")$med)` (`r sprintf("%.0f–%.0f%%", 100*gz("reinforce")$lo, 100*gz("reinforce")$hi)`) of streams reinforce the inherited seasonal contrast, `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100*gz("dampen")$med)` dampen it, `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100*gz("reverse")$med)` reverse it; median gain `r sprintf("%.2f", g_med)`.
-   **Implication.** Beaver-engineering adds about one fifth of the seasonal DOC signal in summer and nothing in winter, and it does not shift the seasonal contrast in one direction — it redistributes it stream by stream. Ecologically, beaver ponds are seasonal control points on a regionally inherited signal, not amplifiers of it.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## How @fig-q1 and @fig-R fit together

@fig-q1 and @fig-R are not two conflicting results — they answer two different questions, so one naturally reads as "mostly nothing detectable" and the other as "most streams have a clear sign."

- **@fig-q1 asks: if someone visits a stream and takes one water sample, what would they most likely find?** This is a single field visit — the way almost every published beaver–DOC study, including the ones this manuscript is compared against, actually samples. The answer: mostly nothing an ecologist would call a real change.
- **@fig-R asks: what is each stream's true relative response, according to the best estimate the model can produce from everything it knows?** This is the paper's actual result — it does not simulate a single field visit, it reports the model's estimate of the real value. The answer: most streams have a clear sign.

Both questions are legitimate and both answers are correct; they are simply not the same question. (The technical reason the two differ — one reports a simulated single observation, the other reports the model's own estimate — is a Methods-level detail and does not need to be repeated at every figure.) For consistency, applying @fig-q1's "no real change" logic to $R_{summer}$ (a $\pm$0.1 band, matching the grey band already drawn in panel (b)) still leaves only `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100*rz("negligible")$med)` of streams with no detectable response, versus `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100*rz("source")$med)` source and `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100*rz("sink")$med)` sink.

Methods sentence: state once that Figure 1a reports the posterior *predictive* distribution of a single new sampling (so it includes the instrument error), while $R_s$, $B$ and $G$ are computed from each stream's posterior *parameter* estimate (the model's estimate of the true concentration).
:::

# 6. Q4 — Intensity of beaver-engineering and the response

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Question:** Is the local response ordered by the intensity of beaver-engineering — the number of dams and the water residence time — or by something else?
:::

Figure 2b ranks the streams by their own response. Here the same per-stream posteriors of $R_{summer}$ and $G$ are placed on the two gradients of beaver-engineering intensity we measured, and the ordering is estimated with a Bayesian model rather than a correlation coefficient: for each response and each gradient, a Student-*t* regression of the response (on the same pseudo-log scale as the figure axis, $t(x) = \operatorname{asinh}(x/0.2)/\ln 10$) on the standardized gradient, in which each stream enters with its posterior median and its posterior standard deviation as a known measurement error (`se()` in brms). The slope $\beta$ is the ordering: $P(\beta > 0)$ is the posterior probability that the response increases along the gradient.

**Manuscript placement: Appendix S1 (Figure S12), with one sentence in the Results.**

```{r fig-intensity}
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "**Relative response and seasonal gain against the intensity of beaver-engineering.** Each point is a stream: posterior median of $R_{summer}$ (top row) or $G$ (bottom row) with 66% (thick) and 95% (thin) credible intervals, against the number of dams (left; jittered) and the summer water residence time (right; log axis). Colours as in Figure 2: source / sink / no-evidence for $R_{summer}$; reinforce / dampen / reverse / no-evidence for $G$ (classified at posterior probability 0.90). The vertical axes are linear between −0.1 and 0.1 and logarithmic beyond. The black line and band are the posterior median and 95% credible interval of a Bayesian Student-t regression of the response (pseudo-log scale) on the standardized gradient, with each stream's posterior standard deviation as its measurement error, drawn back on the response scale; each panel title gives its slope $\\beta$ (posterior median [95% credible interval]) and $P(\\beta > 0)$. $R_s$, $G$, $B$ and $S$ are defined in @tbl-variables."
library(brms)
# covariates per analysed stream: number of dams and summer water residence time (from m6)
cov <- read.csv(here("data", "processed", "m6.csv")) |> filter(season == "summer") |>
  select(site, beaver_territory, n_dams, wrt = water_res_time)
cv <- LR$d |> select(site, beaver_territory) |> left_join(cov, by = c("site", "beaver_territory"))
# per-stream classes for colouring (same rules as Figure 2)
r_class <- cls(colMeans(R_s > 0))
g_class <- apply(G_m, 2, function(g) {
  p <- c(reinforce = mean(g > 0), dampen = mean(g > -1 & g < 0), reverse = mean(g < -1))
  if (max(p) > 0.90) names(p)[which.max(p)] else "no-evidence" })
# the pseudo-log transform used on the figure axis (scales::pseudo_log_trans, sigma = 0.1)
plog <- function(x) asinh(x / 0.2) / log(10)
# Bayesian ordering: Student-t regression of the transformed response on the standardized
# gradient, each stream weighted by its own posterior uncertainty (known se)
slope_fit <- function(M, x, tag) {
  ok <- !is.na(x); TM <- plog(M[, ok])
  dd <- tibble(y = apply(TM, 2, median), se_y = apply(TM, 2, sd), x = as.numeric(scale(x[ok])))
  brm(bf(y | se(se_y, sigma = TRUE) ~ 1 + x), data = dd, family = student(),
      prior = c(prior(normal(0, 1), class = "b"), prior(normal(0, 2), class = "Intercept"),
                prior(student_t(3, 0, 1), class = "sigma"), prior(gamma(2, 0.1), class = "nu")),
      chains = 4, iter = 3000, warmup = 1000, seed = 7, backend = "cmdstanr", refresh = 0,
      file = here("results", "models_fit", paste0("intensity_", tag)))
}
fits <- list(R_dams = slope_fit(R_s, cv$n_dams, "R_dams"), R_wrt = slope_fit(R_s, log10(cv$wrt), "R_wrt"),
             G_dams = slope_fit(G_m, cv$n_dams, "G_dams"), G_wrt = slope_fit(G_m, log10(cv$wrt), "G_wrt"))
beta <- lapply(fits, function(f) as_draws_df(f)$b_x)
b_lab <- function(b) sprintf("beta = %.2f [%.2f, %.2f], P(beta > 0) = %.2f", median(b), quantile(b, .025), quantile(b, .975), mean(b > 0))
qs <- function(M) tibble(med = apply(M, 2, median), lo95 = apply(M, 2, quantile, .025), hi95 = apply(M, 2, quantile, .975),
                         lo66 = apply(M, 2, quantile, .17), hi66 = apply(M, 2, quantile, .83))
rpal <- c(add = "#3B9AD1", remove = "#E8603C", none = "grey60")
rlab <- c(add = "source", remove = "sink", none = "no-evidence")
gpal2 <- c(reinforce = "#8856A7", dampen = "#41AB5D", reverse = "#B5651D", `no-evidence` = "grey60")
inv_plog <- function(y) 0.2 * sinh(y * log(10))   # back from the pseudo-log scale
# posterior regression line of the slope model, drawn on the original scale of the response
fit_line <- function(fit, x_raw, logx) {
  ok <- !is.na(x_raw); xr <- if (logx) log10(x_raw[ok]) else x_raw[ok]
  grid <- seq(min(xr), max(xr), length.out = 60)
  nd <- tibble(x = (grid - mean(xr)) / sd(xr), se_y = 0)
  ep <- posterior_epred(fit, newdata = nd)                  # draws x grid, pseudo-log scale
  tibble(x = if (logx) 10^grid else grid, med = inv_plog(apply(ep, 2, median)),
         lo = inv_plog(apply(ep, 2, quantile, .025)), hi = inv_plog(apply(ep, 2, quantile, .975)))
}
panel <- function(M, x, xlab, class, pal, labs_, ylab, sub, fit, logx = FALSE) {
  d <- qs(M) |> mutate(x = x, class = factor(class, levels = names(pal)))
  pos <- if (logx) "identity" else position_jitter(width = .15, height = 0, seed = 1)
  ln <- fit_line(fit, x, logx)
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(x = x, y = med)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey45") +
    geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lo95, ymax = hi95, colour = class), alpha = .45, linewidth = 0.4, position = pos) +
    geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lo66, ymax = hi66, colour = class), alpha = .8, linewidth = 0.9, position = pos) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = class), size = 1.6, position = pos) +
    geom_ribbon(data = ln, aes(x = x, ymin = lo, ymax = hi), inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "black", alpha = .15) +
    geom_line(data = ln, aes(x = x, y = med), inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.9) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = pal, labels = labs_, breaks = names(pal), name = NULL) +
    scale_y_continuous(trans = psl, breaks = c(-10, -1, -0.1, 0, 0.1, 1, 10)) +
    labs(x = xlab, y = ylab, subtitle = sub) + theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "top", plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10))
  if (logx) p + scale_x_log10() else p
}
ylab_R <- expression(R[summer] == frac(DOC[list(down, summer)] - DOC[list(up, summer)], "|" * DOC[list(up, summer)] - DOC[list(up, winter)] * "|"))
ylab_G <- expression(G == frac(Delta * DOC[summer] - Delta * DOC[winter], DOC[list(up, summer)] - DOC[list(up, winter)]))
p1 <- panel(R_s, cv$n_dams, "Number of dams", r_class, rpal, rlab, ylab_R, b_lab(beta$R_dams), fits$R_dams)
p2 <- panel(R_s, cv$wrt, "Water residence time in summer (s)", r_class, rpal, rlab, ylab_R, b_lab(beta$R_wrt), fits$R_wrt, logx = TRUE)
p3 <- panel(G_m, cv$n_dams, "Number of dams", g_class, gpal2, names(gpal2), ylab_G, b_lab(beta$G_dams), fits$G_dams)
p4 <- panel(G_m, cv$wrt, "Water residence time in summer (s)", g_class, gpal2, names(gpal2), ylab_G, b_lab(beta$G_wrt), fits$G_wrt, logx = TRUE)
figI <- (p1 + p2) / (p3 + p4) + plot_layout(guides = "collect") + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a") &
  theme(legend.position = "top")
ggsave(here("results", "figures", "plan", "fig_intensity.png"), figI, width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 300)
figI
bt <- function(k) sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", median(beta[[k]]), quantile(beta[[k]], .025), quantile(beta[[k]], .975))
bp <- function(k) sprintf("%.2f", mean(beta[[k]] > 0))
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Key message of @fig-intensity

-   **Water residence time orders the summer response, weakly.** $\beta$ = `r bt("R_wrt")` per SD of log residence time, $P(\beta > 0)$ = `r bp("R_wrt")`.
-   **The number of dams does not.** $\beta$ = `r bt("R_dams")`, $P(\beta > 0)$ = `r bp("R_dams")`.
-   **The seasonal gain is ordered by neither.** `r bt("G_dams")` (dams) and `r bt("G_wrt")` (residence time).
-   **Implication.** Longer impoundment favours DOC release in summer (the stream-level counterpart of the Q2 path residence time → phytoplankton → DOC), but sources, sinks, reinforcing and dampening streams occur at every level of engineering: the intensity of beaver-engineering sets the stage, it does not decide the sign. Sentence for Appendix S1 (Figure S12) as above.
:::

# 7. Spatial coherence of the seasonal contrasts

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Question** (Discussion support)**:** *the inherited seasonal contrast is generated over whole floodplains — is the modification that beaver-engineering imposes on it organised at the same regional scale, or is it stream-specific?* The answer decides how the Discussion frames beaver-engineering: if $B$ were regionally coherent, beaver-engineered streams would act together as a landscape-scale control on the seasonal DOC signal; if $B$ is spatially incoherent, each beaver-engineered stream is an independent local control point on a regional signal — the framing the manuscript title claims.
:::

For each stream we correlate its value with the mean of its 8 nearest neighbours (Spearman), computed on every posterior draw of the concentrations, so the coherence estimate carries the full uncertainty. $T = \text{DOC}_{down,summer} - \text{DOC}_{down,winter}$ is the **downstream seasonal contrast** ($T = S + B$).

**Manuscript placement: Appendix S1 (Figure S11), plus one sentence in the Discussion.**

```{r fig-spatial}
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-cap: "**Spatial coherence of the inherited seasonal contrast $S$, the beaver seasonal modification $B$ and the downstream seasonal contrast $T$.** Posterior distribution of the Spearman correlation between each stream's value and the mean of its 8 nearest neighbours, computed on every posterior draw of the concentrations. Point: median; bars: 66% and 95% credible intervals; dashed line: no spatial coherence. $S$ and $B$ are defined in @tbl-variables ($T = S + B$)."
# stream coordinates (longitude, latitude of the upstream sampling point)
co <- read.csv(here("data", "processed", "m6.csv")) |> distinct(site, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  select(site, lon = x_upstream, lat = y_upstream)
d2 <- left_join(LR$d, co, by = "site")
# planar distances in km (adequate at the scale of Switzerland)
kmx <- (d2$lon - mean(d2$lon)) * 111.32 * cos(mean(d2$lat) * pi / 180)
kmy <- (d2$lat - mean(d2$lat)) * 110.57
D <- as.matrix(dist(cbind(kmx, kmy))); diag(D) <- Inf
# for each stream, the indices of its 8 nearest neighbours (fixed across draws)
nb <- t(apply(D, 1, function(r) order(r)[1:8]))
# mean of the neighbours' values, for one vector of stream values
nbmean <- function(v) rowMeans(matrix(v[as.vector(nb)], nrow = length(v)))
# one Spearman correlation per posterior draw -> a posterior distribution of coherence
rho_draw <- function(M) apply(M, 1, function(v) cor(v, nbmean(v), method = "spearman"))
T_m <- S_m + B_m   # downstream seasonal contrast, per draw
sp <- bind_rows(tibble(q = "inherited seasonal contrast S", rho = rho_draw(S_m)),
                tibble(q = "beaver seasonal modification B", rho = rho_draw(B_m)),
                tibble(q = "downstream seasonal contrast T", rho = rho_draw(T_m))) |>
  mutate(q = factor(q, levels = c("beaver seasonal modification B", "downstream seasonal contrast T",
                                  "inherited seasonal contrast S")))
sp_med <- sp |> group_by(q) |> summarise(m = median(rho))
ps <- ggplot(sp, aes(x = rho, y = q)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey45") +
  stat_halfeye(.width = c(.66, .95), point_interval = "median_qi", fill = "grey80") +
  labs(x = "Spearman correlation with the mean of the 8 nearest neighbours", y = NULL) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
ggsave(here("results", "figures", "plan", "fig_spatial.png"), ps, width = 8, height = 3.5, dpi = 300)
ps
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Key message of @fig-spatial

-   **The inherited seasonal contrast is regional.** Neighbour correlation of $S$: `r sprintf("%.2f", sp_med$m[sp_med$q == "inherited seasonal contrast S"])`.
-   **The downstream contrast inherits that structure.** $T$: `r sprintf("%.2f", sp_med$m[sp_med$q == "downstream seasonal contrast T"])`.
-   **The beaver seasonal modification is local.** $B$: `r sprintf("%.2f", sp_med$m[sp_med$q == "beaver seasonal modification B"])`, credible interval spanning zero.
-   **Implication.** Neighbouring streams inherit the same seasonal signal but do not modify it in the same way: each beaver-engineered stream reinforces, dampens or reverses a regionally organised signal on its own terms. This rules out a regional gradient masquerading as a beaver effect, and it is the empirical basis for calling beaver ponds *local* control points. Sentence for the Discussion as above.
:::

# 8. Model validation: out-of-sample prediction

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Question:** Can the SCM predict downstream DOC, and the local change, at a stream it has not seen?
:::

The manuscript claims that the model can be used to anticipate the effect of beaver-engineering on stream DOC in Switzerland. That claim needs an out-of-sample test. Two are reported for `downstream_DOC_me`: (i) Pareto-smoothed importance-sampling leave-one-out cross-validation (PSIS-LOO), in which every observed downstream concentration is predicted as if it had been left out of the fit; and (ii) a hold-out test, in which the SCM is refitted on 80% of the streams and predicts downstream DOC at the remaining 20% (`r if (file.exists(here("results","me_holdout.rds"))) readRDS(here("results","me_holdout.rds"))$n_test_streams else "…"` streams), which it has never seen. At an unseen stream the site effect is unknown and the mediators are mostly unmeasured (they enter at their mean), so the hold-out prediction is what a user in Switzerland would actually have: upstream DOC, the dams, the channel gradient and solar radiation. For both tests, the derived $\Delta\text{DOC}$ is scored as well, because that is the quantity the claim is about; it is computed per posterior draw $d$ and sampling $i$ as

$$
\Delta\text{DOC}^{(d)}_i = \mu^{(d)}_i - \text{DOC}_{up,i}
$$ {#eq-derived-plan}

with $\mu_i$ the SCM's expected downstream DOC. Details of the derivation in `notebook/correspondence/scm_outcome_choice.qmd`.

**Manuscript placement: Appendix S1 (Figure S13), with one sentence in the Methods and one in the Discussion.**

```{r validation}
#| echo: false
pred_path <- here("results", "me_predictions.rds"); hold_path <- here("results", "me_holdout.rds")
have_pred <- file.exists(pred_path); have_hold <- file.exists(hold_path)
if (have_pred) P <- readRDS(pred_path)
if (have_hold) {
  H <- readRDS(hold_path)
  y_h <- H$obs_o_test; mu_h <- H$mu_o_test; q_h <- H$q_o_test
  d_obs_h <- H$obs_d_test; d_pred_h <- H$dd_test_pred_med; q_dh <- H$dd_q_test
}
if (have_pred && have_hold) {
  met <- function(y, mu, q = NULL) c(R2 = 1 - sum((y - mu)^2) / sum((y - mean(y))^2), RMSE = sqrt(mean((y - mu)^2)),
                                     cover = if (is.null(q)) NA else mean(y >= q[1, ] & y <= q[2, ]))
  # in-sample, full model (all 158 streams, site effects known)
  mu_in <- colMeans(P$O$ep_sub[, P$obsO]); q_in <- apply(P$O$pp_sub[, P$obsO], 2, quantile, c(.05, .95))
  in_full <- met(P$y_out, mu_in, q_in)
  ib_full <- match(P$both, P$obsO)
  d_in_full <- met(P$d_obs, colMeans(P$O$ep_sub[, P$both]) - P$up_both, apply(sweep(P$O$pp_sub[, P$both], 2, P$up_both), 2, quantile, c(.05, .95)))
  # LOO, full model
  loo_full <- met(P$y_out, P$O$mu_loo, P$O$q_loo)
  loo_d <- met(P$d_obs, P$O$mu_loo[ib_full] - P$up_both, P$O$dd_q_loo)
  n_all_streams <- length(unique(read.csv(here("data", "processed", "m6.csv"))$site))
  n_train_streams <- n_all_streams - H$n_test_streams
  f2 <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f", x); fp <- function(x) sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * x)
  val_msg <- sprintf("- **Downstream DOC at an unseen stream is predictable.** Hold-out R² = %.2f, RMSE %.2f mg L⁻¹ (spread of the data %.2f), 90%% predictive intervals containing %.0f%% of the unseen observations — calibrated.\n- **No overfitting.** In-sample R² %.2f, leave-one-out %.2f (full model); %.2f in sample for the hold-out fit. The R² across all samplings is capped by a few very high concentrations in the heavy tail (RMSE %.1f against a spread of %.1f), not by unseen streams.\n- **The local change is not predictable.** Derived ΔDOC: hold-out R² = %.2f, RMSE %.2f against %.2f for predicting its mean.",
    H$O_out["R2"], H$O_out["RMSE"], H$O_out["RMSE_null"], 100 * H$O_out["cover90"], in_full["R2"], loo_full["R2"], H$O_in["R2"], loo_full["RMSE"], sd(P$y_out), H$Od_out["R2"], H$Od_out["RMSE"], H$Od_out["RMSE_null"])
  kable(tribble(
    ~Quantity, ~Test, ~`In / out of sample`, ~`R²`, ~`RMSE (mg L⁻¹)`, ~`RMSE of predicting the mean`, ~`90% interval coverage`,
    "Downstream DOC", sprintf("Full model, all %d samplings", length(P$y_out)), "in-sample", f2(in_full["R2"]), f2(in_full["RMSE"]), f2(sd(P$y_out)), fp(in_full["cover"]),
    "Downstream DOC", "Full model, PSIS-LOO", "out-of-sample", f2(loo_full["R2"]), f2(loo_full["RMSE"]), f2(sd(P$y_out)), fp(loo_full["cover"]),
    "Downstream DOC", sprintf("Hold-out fit, %d training streams", n_train_streams), "in-sample", f2(H$O_in["R2"]), f2(H$O_in["RMSE"]), f2(H$O_in["RMSE_null"]), fp(H$O_in["cover90"]),
    "Downstream DOC", sprintf("Hold-out fit, %d unseen streams (%d samplings)", H$n_test_streams, length(y_h)), "out-of-sample", f2(H$O_out["R2"]), f2(H$O_out["RMSE"]), f2(H$O_out["RMSE_null"]), fp(H$O_out["cover90"]),
    "Derived ΔDOC", sprintf("Full model, all %d samplings", length(P$d_obs)), "in-sample", f2(d_in_full["R2"]), f2(d_in_full["RMSE"]), f2(sd(P$d_obs)), fp(d_in_full["cover"]),
    "Derived ΔDOC", "Full model, PSIS-LOO", "out-of-sample", f2(loo_d["R2"]), f2(loo_d["RMSE"]), f2(sd(P$d_obs)), fp(loo_d["cover"]),
    "Derived ΔDOC", "Hold-out fit, training streams", "in-sample", f2(H$Od_in["R2"]), f2(H$Od_in["RMSE"]), f2(H$Od_in["RMSE_null"]), "—",
    "Derived ΔDOC", "Hold-out fit, unseen streams", "out-of-sample", f2(H$Od_out["R2"]), f2(H$Od_out["RMSE"]), f2(H$Od_out["RMSE_null"]), fp(mean(d_obs_h >= q_dh[1, ] & d_obs_h <= q_dh[2, ]))),
    caption = sprintf("Predictive performance of downstream_DOC_me, in and out of sample. In-sample predictions include the stream random effects (the model has seen the stream); out-of-sample predictions do not. Hold-out fit: max R-hat %.3f.", H$rhat["down"]))
} else { cat("Predictions not yet computed (notebook/fitting/me_predictions.R, notebook/fitting/me_holdout.R)."); val_msg <- "- pending" }
```

```{r fig-holdout}
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-cap: "**Hold-out test of downstream_DOC_me.** The model was refitted on 80% of the streams and predicts the other 20%, which it has never seen. (a) Predicted (posterior mean, with 90% predictive interval) against observed downstream DOC at the unseen streams; dashed line: 1:1. (b) The derived local response, predicted downstream DOC minus upstream DOC, against the observed ΔDOC at the same samplings, with its own 90% predictive interval. $\\Delta\\text{DOC}_s$ is defined in @tbl-variables."
if (have_hold) {
  pa <- ggplot(tibble(y = y_h, mu = mu_h, lo = q_h[1, ], hi = q_h[2, ]), aes(y, mu)) +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey45") +
    geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), colour = "grey70", alpha = .6) + geom_point(size = 1.6, colour = "#3B9AD1") +
    labs(x = expression("Observed downstream DOC (mg "*L^-1*")"), y = expression("Predicted downstream DOC (mg "*L^-1*")")) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 12) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
  pb <- ggplot(tibble(o = d_obs_h, p = d_pred_h, lo = q_dh[1, ], hi = q_dh[2, ]), aes(o, p)) +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey45") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey80") + geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey80") +
    geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), colour = "grey70", alpha = .6) + geom_point(size = 1.6, colour = "#3B9AD1") +
    labs(x = expression("Observed "*Delta*"DOC (mg "*L^-1*")"), y = expression("Predicted "*Delta*"DOC (mg "*L^-1*")")) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 12) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
  figH <- pa + pb + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a")
  ggsave(here("results", "figures", "plan", "fig_holdout.png"), figH, width = 9, height = 4.5, dpi = 300)
```
